Texas Tech University (TTU) K-12 Support — Counselor Portal Frequently Asked Questions

Answer

For Counselors

Texas Tech K-12 Support can help counselors with admissions, registration, Canvas, and basic technical issues. Use our support portal to open Frequently Asked Questions or chat live: Open the Support Portal (opens in new tab). For phone help call 1-800-692-6877.

Abbreviations used on this page are defined in the Glossary / Definitions section. See Glossary / Definitions.

Commencement

Texas Tech K-12 celebrates graduates from the full-Time Diploma Program each year during the traditional graduation season. A schedule for upcoming graduation ceremonies can be found on the Graduation Preparation page (opens in new tab) on the Texas Tech K-12 website. Graduating seniors should plan to complete their coursework and final exams at least two weeks in advance of the graduation date to ensure they are included in their desired graduating class. Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma Program offers class rings, invitations, and caps and gowns through Herff Jones Company (opens in new tab) –

West Texas Graduation Services (opens in new tab).

Contact them by phone at +1-806-744-7337, by fax to +1-806-744-1744, by email to info@westtexasgrad.com.

I would like to enroll in the Texas Tech High School Diploma Program

If you are interested in enrolling in the Texas Tech K-12 program, we ask that you please complete the intake form (opens in new tab). In the application page, we ask that you please select "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form" (TTU K-12 Intake Form). On page 2 of the application you will be asked to select the most appropriate program for your student:

Full-time Tuition-Free Diploma Program (TX Residents Only) (opens in new tab)

The State of Texas has designated Texas Tech K-12 eligible to receive state funds. As a result, beginning in August 2021, we will offer a tuition-free K-12 online academic program available only to Texas Residents!  *Note: There are requirements (opens in new tab)to which you must adhere if you wish to be included in the tuition-free program. You will need to withdraw from your local school district to attend Texas Tech K-12 full-time tuition-free program.

Please read carefully: To apply to this program:

Step 1: it must be consistent with your academic needs,

Step 2: you must be a Texas resident under the age of 25 and provide Proof of Residency (opens in new tab),

Step 3: you must provide a copy of your birth certificate,

Supporting Schools to Help Students Thrive

Texas Tech K-12 offers flexible, year-round solutions designed to supplement your school district's curriculum and support students in reaching their goals.

Unique Individual Electronic mail Address

Texas Tech K-12 requires an electronic mail address for each student, and a separate, unique electronic mail address for at least one parent/guardian. Electronic mail addresses cannot be shared. This ensures proper login access and that all communications and password resets go to the correct recipient.

Allow listed Requirements

If you are using a personal electronic mail address and are not receiving electronic mail from Texas Tech K-12, first check your Junk or Spam folder. If the email is located there, move it to your Inbox. Doing so typically marks the sender as safe, increasing the likelihood that future electronic mail from Texas Tech K-12 will be delivered directly to your inbox.

If a student is using a district-provided email address, the district Information Technology department must allow list the following information to ensure delivery of the system.

Introduction

Welcome to Texas Tech K-12! As a District Partnership Student, this page is designed to guide you through the Focus Student Portal.

If you have any questions, our Support Team may be reached via 1-800-692-6877 or by submitting a Support Ticket.

We look forward to supporting you with your Academic Journey.

Step 1: Computer: Modern device (≤5 years old) with 4 Gigabyte Random Access Memory (8–16 Gigabyte recommended), 250 Gigabyte+ hard drive, webcam, microphone, speakers, and updated antivirus software

Step 2: Operating Systems: Windows 10+, mac operating system 11+, Chrome operating system, or Linux (Ubuntu 18.04+)

Step 3: Browsers (latest versions):

Step 4: Google Chrome (required for online exams)

Step 5: Mozilla Firefox

Step 6: Microsoft Edge

Step 11: JavaScript enabled

Step 12: Cookies enabled

Step 14: Advertisement blockers disabled

Q: What is Texas Tech K-12's policy on class rank?

A: Class rank shall not be calculated or reported except for students in the Top 10% of a given class as required by state law. This change is in place for students enrolling in TTU K-12 after August 1, 2021.

Texas Tech K-12 High School Program - Full-Time

Texas Tech K-12 is a state-approved option for students who need or desire the flexibility of a distance education to earn their high school diploma. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan.

Adult Learning Program (ALP/TWC)

Texas Tech K-12 is committed to supporting lifelong learning and educational advancement. While we do not currently offer an adult high school diploma or General Educational Development preparation program, we understand the importance of these pathways and the opportunities they can provide.

Adult learners often seek options to complete a high school education or prepare for the General Educational Development exam in flexible, accessible ways. Programs like these can support individuals in reaching personal, educational, and professional goals by offering coursework, skill development, and preparation resources.

Should Texas Tech K-12 offer an adult education program in the future, it would likely include online coursework, potential support services, and flexible pacing to help adult learners succeed.

Potential Program Features May Include:

Step 1: High school credit completion or General Educational Development exam preparation

Step 2: Online learning options

Step 3: Support with tutoring and academic planning

Step 4: College and career readiness resources
